about.headline: An honest space for discussion, bridging dynamic visuals with sharp literacy.
about.lede: EGI Media was born from a passion to create a collaborative space for exploring diverse perspectives without being patronizing.
about.pullQuote: Objectivity and creativity in every piece — informative, yet enjoyable to follow.
paragraphs: Born from a passion to create an honest space for discussion, this media became a collaborative platform for processing diverse perspectives without being patronizing. Its main focus is bridging dynamic visual content with sharp literacy.

The YouTube channel is the main engine through a Podcast program that explores a range of topics in depth. Not stopping at audio-visual content, every key point and interesting detail is further developed through articles on the website. Its coverage is broad and relevant to today's lifestyle — from the dynamics of Politics, developments in Technology, sportsmanship in Sport, Entertainment reviews, to Travel exploration.

EGI Media prioritizes objectivity and creativity in every piece of content it produces. The goal is simple: to be a reference that is informative yet enjoyable to follow. Amid the fast flow of information, integrity and accuracy remain the main foundation, while continuously adapting to current trends. Every idea broadcast and every word written is expected to bring new color and spark the birth of other fresh ideas.

privacy.headline: Privacy Policy
privacy.lede: EGI Media respects your privacy. This policy explains how we collect, use, store, and protect personal information when you use our services.

sections.title: Scope
paragraphs: This Privacy Policy applies to the EGI Media website, newsletters, and related digital services we operate.
By using our services, you acknowledge the practices described in this policy.

sections.title: Information we collect
paragraphs: We may collect information you provide directly, such as your name and email address when you subscribe to a newsletter or contact us.
We may also collect technical data automatically, including IP address, device type, browser, pages visited, and usage data that helps us understand site performance.

sections.title: How we use information
paragraphs: We use information to provide and improve our services, send newsletters or communications you request, respond to inquiries, and maintain the security and reliability of the platform.
We may use aggregated or anonymized data for editorial analysis and product development without personally identifying you.

sections.title: Legal bases and legitimate purposes

Where processing requires consent, we will request it before processing data for that purpose.

sections.title: Cookies and similar technologies
paragraphs: Our website may use cookies or similar technologies for browsing experience, language preferences, and performance measurement.
You can configure your browser to refuse cookies. However, some site features may not work optimally without certain cookies.

sections.title: Sharing of information
paragraphs: We do not sell your personal data. We may share information with trusted service providers who help us operate (such as hosting, analytics, or email delivery), only as needed for those services.
We may also disclose information when required by law, or to protect the rights, safety, and integrity of EGI Media and our users.

sections.title: Retention and security
paragraphs: We retain personal data for as long as needed for the purposes described in this policy, or as required by law.
We apply reasonable technical and organizational measures to protect data from unauthorized access, alteration, or disclosure. However, no internet transmission is completely secure.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: Subject to applicable law, you may have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of certain personal data we hold about you.
You may also unsubscribe from newsletters at any time via the unsubscribe link in emails, or by contacting us.

sections.title: Third-party services
paragraphs: Our services may link to third-party platforms such as YouTube or social media. Their privacy policies apply to data collected on those platforms.
We encourage you to review each third party’s privacy policy before providing information.

sections.title: Children
paragraphs: Our services are not directed to children under the age defined by local law without parental or guardian supervision.
If you believe we have received data from a child without appropriate permission, contact us so we can review and delete it if necessary.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. The latest version will be published on this page with the update date.
Continued use of the services after changes take effect means you acknowledge the updated practices.

pedomanSiber.headline: Cyber Media News Guidelines
pedomanSiber.adoptedOn: Press Council Regulation No. 1/Peraturan-DP/III/2012 · Jakarta, 3 February 2012
pedomanSiber.lede: Official Press Council guidelines for managing cyber media professionally in accordance with Law No. 40 of 1999 on the Press and the Journalistic Code of Ethics.
intro: Freedom of opinion, freedom of expression, and freedom of the press are human rights protected by Pancasila, the 1945 Constitution, and the UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights. The presence of cyber media in Indonesia is also part of freedom of opinion, freedom of expression, and freedom of the press.

Cyber media has distinctive characteristics and therefore requires guidelines so that it can be managed professionally, fulfilling its functions, rights, and obligations under Law No. 40 of 1999 on the Press and the Journalistic Code of Ethics. For that reason, the Press Council, together with press organizations, cyber media operators, and the public, adopted the Cyber Media News Guidelines as follows:

items.text: Cyber Media means any form of media that uses the internet and carries out journalistic activities, and that meets the requirements of the Press Law and the Press Company Standards established by the Press Council.

User Generated Content means any content created and/or published by cyber media users, including articles, images, comments, audio, video, and other uploads attached to cyber media, such as blogs, forums, reader or viewer comments, and similar forms.
In principle, every news report must be verified.
News that may harm another party requires verification within the same report to meet the principles of accuracy and balance.
The provision in point (a) above may be excepted, provided that:
children: The news truly involves urgent public interest;
The first source is clearly identified, credible, and competent;
The subject of the news who must be confirmed cannot be located and/or cannot be interviewed;

The media explains to readers that the report still requires further verification, which will be pursued as soon as possible. The explanation appears at the end of the same report, in parentheses and in italics.

items.text: After publishing a report under point (c), the media must continue verification efforts, and once verification is obtained, the results must be included in an updated report with a link to the unverified report.

Cyber media must publish terms and conditions on User Generated Content that do not conflict with Law No. 40 of 1999 on the Press and the Journalistic Code of Ethics, placed clearly and conspicuously.
Cyber media must require every user to register as a member and log in before publishing any form of User Generated Content. Login provisions will be regulated further.
In that registration, cyber media must require users to give written consent that User Generated Content published:
children: Does not contain false, defamatory, sadistic, or obscene content;
Does not contain prejudice or hatred related to ethnicity, religion, race, or inter-group relations (SARA), and does not encourage violence;
Does not contain discriminatory content based on gender or language, and does not demean the dignity of the weak, the poor, the sick, or persons with mental or physical disabilities.

items.text: Cyber media has absolute authority to edit or delete User Generated Content that conflicts with point (c).
Cyber media must provide a complaint mechanism for User Generated Content deemed to violate point (c). The mechanism must be placed where users can easily access it.

Cyber media must edit, delete, and take corrective action on any reported User Generated Content that violates point (c), as soon as reasonably possible and no later than 2 × 24 hours after the complaint is received.
Cyber media that has complied with points (a), (b), (c), and (f) is not burdened with liability for problems arising from published content that violates point (c).
Cyber media is responsible for reported User Generated Content if it fails to take corrective action after the time limit in point (f).

sections.title: Corrections, Retractions, and the Right of Reply

items.text: Corrections, retractions, and the right of reply refer to the Press Law, the Journalistic Code of Ethics, and the Right of Reply Guidelines established by the Press Council.
A correction, retraction, and/or right of reply must be linked to the report being corrected, retracted, or given a right of reply.
Every correction, retraction, and right-of-reply report must state the time it was published.
If a report by one cyber media outlet is disseminated by another, then:
children: The responsibility of the originating cyber media is limited to the report published on that outlet or on media under its technical authority;
A correction made by one cyber media outlet must also be made by other cyber media that quoted the corrected report;

Media that disseminate a report from a cyber media outlet and fail to correct it in line with the correction by the owner and/or originator of the report bear full legal responsibility for all consequences of the uncorrected report.

items.text: Under the Press Law, cyber media that fails to honor the right of reply may be subject to a criminal fine of up to Rp500,000,000 (five hundred million rupiah).

Published news may not be withdrawn because of censorship from parties outside the newsroom, except in matters related to SARA, morality, the future of children, a victim’s traumatic experience, or other special considerations established by the Press Council.
Other cyber media must follow the withdrawal of quoted reports from the original outlet that has withdrawn them.
Withdrawal of a report must be accompanied by reasons and announced to the public.
Cyber media must clearly distinguish news products from advertising.

Every news item/article/content that is an advertisement and/or paid content must include the label "advertorial", "iklan", "ads", "sponsored", or another word explaining that the item is an advertisement.

sections.title: Copyright
paragraphs: Cyber media must respect copyright as regulated under applicable laws and regulations.

sections.title: Publication of the Guidelines
paragraphs: Cyber media must publish these Cyber Media News Guidelines on its platform clearly and conspicuously.

sections.title: Disputes
paragraphs: Final assessment of disputes regarding the implementation of these Cyber Media News Guidelines is resolved by the Press Council.
